description:
WHAT: Offline email checks: RFC-style syntax + normalization, common domain typo "did you mean" (gmial.com -> gmail.com), disposable/temporary domain (bundled CC0 list, ~thousands of domains), role account (info@, sales@), free webmail provider.
WHEN: Fast pre-filtering of signups or lead lists, before paying for email_validate_deliverability.
WHEN NOT: Does NOT check DNS/MX, so it cannot tell whether the domain receives mail; use email_validate_deliverability (paid) for MX/SPF/DMARC.
COST: Free; local, no token.
RETURNS: Paged "email_check" rows; verdict is invalid | risky | unknown, never valid (dns_checked is always false).
BEHAVIOR: No network calls (no DNS/SMTP); synchronous and CPU-bound, no rate limits: 10,000 addresses (the per-call maximum) return in well under a second.
PARAMETERS: emails: each element is parsed on its own (one address per element; a comma-separated list in one element is INVALID_SYNTAX, not split). Before checking, "Name <addr>" is reduced to addr, a leading "mailto:" is dropped, the domain is lowercased (local part keeps its case), a trailing dot is removed and IDN domains are converted to punycode; the normalized value is returned as email, the original as input. Duplicates are not merged: every element yields one row, in input order. Role detection ignores +tags (sales+eu@ counts as sales@) and disposable matching also covers subdomains of listed domains. limit/offset page those rows; meta.summary always counts verdicts over ALL rows, not just the current page.
EXAMPLE: {"emails":["someone@gmial.com"]} -> verdict "risky", reasons ["POSSIBLE_TYPO","DNS_NOT_CHECKED"], did_you_mean "someone@gmail.com".

emails.description: Required. 1-10000 strings, 1-320 chars each, one address per element; bare "jane@acme.com", "Jane <jane@acme.com>" and "mailto:jane@acme.com" forms accepted. Example: ["jane@acme.com","bob@gmial.com"]

limit.description: Optional page size: items to return, integer 1-1000 (default 100). Example: 50

offset.description: Optional zero-based number of items to skip, integer 0-1000000 (default 0); pass nextOffset from the previous response, e.g. 100

name: email_check_syntax

count.description: Number of items in this page

hasMore.description: True if more items exist after this page

nextOffset.description: Offset to pass for the next page, or null

offset.description: Offset of the first item in this page

title: Check email syntax, typos, disposable & role (free)
